 * Given a start and end value, you need to create a list using the 'range' function. The list should

 *
 * @param start the starting value of the range (inclusive)
 * @param end the ending value of the range (exclusive)
 * @param initialElements a list of initial values
 * @return A list containing numbers within the range (start, end), excluding any numbers found in initialElements.
 */
fun listIntersection(start: Int, end: Int, initialElements: List<Int>): List<Int> {

    // Create a list using the range function, with numbers from start to end

    // Remove any numbers from the numbersList that are also present in the initialElements list
    return numbersList.filter { it !in initialElements }

/**
 * Calculates the total material amount for a fashion designer, considering the given parameters.
 *
 * @param unitCost The cost per unit of a material.
 * @param quantity The number of units of the material.
 * @param discountPercentage The percentage of discount applied on the material cost.
 * @param taxPercentage The percentage of tax added on the material cost.
 * @return The total amount of material cost after applying discount and adding tax.
 */
fun calculateTotalMaterialAmount(unitCost: Double, quantity: Int, discountPercentage: Double, taxPercentage: Double): Double {

    // Applying discount
    val discountAmount = unitCost * quantity * discountPercentage / 100
    val discountedUnitCost = unitCost - discountAmount / quantity

    // Adding tax
    val taxAmount = discountedUnitCost * quantity * taxPercentage / 100

    // Calculating total material amount
    val totalAmount = (discountedUnitCost * quantity) + taxAmount

    return totalAmount
}

/**
 * This function finds the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two integers.
 *
 * @param a an integer
 * @param b an integer
 * @return The GCD of 'a' and 'b'
 */
fun gcd(a: Int, b: Int): Int {

    var numA = a
    var numB = b

    while (numB != 0) {
        val temp = numA
        numA = numB
        numB = temp % numB
    }

    return numA
};1

fun createGameObjects(objects: Map<String, Int>, count: Int): List<String> {

        val repeatedObjects = List(count) { obj }  // List repetition

fun find(r: Node, c1: String, c2: String): Node? {
    val noList = emptyList<Node>()
    var c1Path: List<Node> = noList
    var c2Path: List<Node> = noList
    r.traverse { n, path ->
        if (n.name == c1) c1Path = path
        if (n.name == c2) c2Path = path
        c1Path === noList || c2Path === noList
    }

    //if (c1Path === noList || c2Path === noList) return null

    val minSize = minOf(c1Path.size, c2Path.size)
    if (minSize <= 1) return r

    c1Path = c1Path.take(minSize)
    c2Path = c2Path.take(minSize)
    var i = 0
    while (i <= minSize - 2) {
        if (c1Path[i] == c2Path[i] && c1Path[i + 1] != c2Path[i + 1]) break
        i++
    }

    return c1Path[i]
};0

fun calculateDistances(playerX: Double, playerY: Double, enemyPositions: List<Pair<Double, Double>>): List<Double> {

    val distances = mutableListOf<Double>()
    for ((enemyX, enemyY) in enemyPositions) {
        val distance = Math.sqrt((playerX - enemyX).pow(2) + (playerY - enemyY).pow(2))
        distances.add(distance)
    }
    return distances

/**
 * Given a list of photos, where each photo is represented by a set of tags,
 * and a set of tags, return a set of all the common tags that appear in all the photos.
 *
 * @param photos List of photos, where each photo is represented by a set of tags.
 * @param tags Set of tags.
 * @return Set of all the common tags.
 *
 * Example:
 * val photos = setOf(setOf("landscape", "nature"),
 *                    setOf("portrait", "people", "nature"),
 *                    setOf("sunset", "landscape", "nature", "color"))
 *
 * val tags = setOf("landscape", "nature")
 *
 * getCommonTags(photos, tags) => setOf("landscape", "nature")
 */
fun getCommonTags(photos: List<Set<String>>, tags: Set<String>): Set<String> {

    val commonTags = tags.toMutableSet()
    for (photo in photos) {
        commonTags.retainAll(photo)
    }
    return commonTags
};1

fun intersectionListComp(A: List<Int>, B: List<Int>): List<Int> {

    return A.filter { it in B }

/**
 * Finds the intersection of two sets.
 *
 * @param set1 The first set.
 * @param set2 The second set.
 * @return A new set containing the common elements found in both sets.
 *
 * Examples:
 * val set1 = setOf(1, 2, 3, 4)
 * val set2 = setOf(3, 4, 5, 6)
 * intersectionOfSets(set1, set2) // Output: [3, 4]
 * val set3 = setOf(10, 20, 30, 40)
 * val set4 = setOf(30, 40, 50, 60)
 * intersectionOfSets(set3, set4) // Output: [30, 40]
 */
fun intersectionOfSets(set1: Set<Int>, set2: Set<Int>): Set<Int> {

    val intersectionSet = mutableSetOf<Int>()
    for (element in set1) {
        if (element in set2) {
            intersectionSet.add(element)
        }
    }
    return intersectionSet
};1

fun findNumberSum(listOfNumbers: List<Int>): Int {

    val negativeNumbers = listOfNumbers.filter { it < 0 }  // Filtering out negative numbers
    val numberSum = negativeNumbers.sum()  // Calculating the sum of negative numbers
    return numberSum
};1

    var points = 0

    if (me == 0 && (opponent == 2)) points += 6
    if (me == 1 && (opponent == 0)) points += 6
    if (me == 2 && (opponent == 1)) points += 6

/**
 * This function takes a photo and returns its type based on its resolution.
 *
 * @param photo A pair containing the width and height of the photo in pixels.
 * @return The type of the photo ('landscape', 'portrait', or 'square').
 *
 * Examples:
 * findPhotosType(Pair(800, 600)) // 'landscape'
 * findPhotosType(Pair(600, 800)) // 'portrait'
 * findPhotosType(Pair(500, 500)) // 'square'
 */
fun findPhotosType(photo: Pair<Int, Int>): String {

    val (width, height) = photo

    return when {
        width > height -> "landscape"
        width < height -> "portrait"
        else -> "square"
    }
};1
